title: User-driven Response Modules — lab notes
body:
Context:
Quick brain dump — idea for letting end users (developers or advanced end-app authors) compose small, composable response "modules" that the runtime can assemble at inference time. Think of tiny behavior snippets that are triggered by signals and stitched into outputs with quality/cost controls.

Why?
- Product problem: apps need predictable cost/latency but also want flexible behavior (summaries + citations + style transforms + persona hints). Implementing each combination in app code is brittle and expensive.
- Hypothesis: a small DSL + module registry + runtime-aware stitching can reduce app complexity and improve reusability while allowing Redwood to optimize execution (cache, batch, quantized variants).

Primary goals (MVP):
- Allow devs to register 1–5 small response modules (max ~120 tokens output each) with triggers and configuration.
- Runtime picks modules for a request, composes them with a composition plan, executes efficiently (prefers cached or lower-cost variant when safe).
- Provide telemetry showing per-module cost/latency/quality and per-route module usage.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Not building a full marketplace or 3rd-party moderation flows yet.
- Not supporting arbitrarily deep recursive modules.

Core concepts (working names):
- Module: tiny transformation or content generator. Contains metadata (id, owner, trigger predicates, tier preferences, fallback policy, estimated token footprint) and a body (prompt template / structured output spec / function binding).
- Composition plan: ordered list of modules + joins + optional scaffolding templates. Produced by a planner service (lightweight).
- Execution variant: compiled runtime profile for a module (high-fidelity model, quantized low-cost model, cached snippet).
- Safety/fallback policy: for each module, define what to do if it fails (skip, replace with default text, call fallback module).

Example modules (sketch):
- summary-short: trigger=customer_message_length>512, output=bullet-summary (<=60 tokens), fallback=short-sentence
- citation-finder: trigger=contains_url OR require-sources=true, output=source-list structured JSON, fallback=mark-unknown
- humor-tone: trigger=user_prefers_tone=light, output=wrap-in-mild-humor, fallback=no-op

Simple user story set:
- As a product engineer, I can register a module with a prompt template and a trigger predicate so the app can opt-in to extra behavior only when needed.
- As a runtime, I can choose the cheapest execution variant that meets module constraints (latency SLO, fidelity label).
- As an operator, I can see per-module cost and error rates and disable problematic modules across customers.
- As an app, I can pin a route to allow only a subset of modules (whitelist) and set a budget for total added tokens from modules per request.

API surfaces (MVP sketch):
- POST /modules  — create module (metadata + template + triggers)
- GET /modules/{id} — fetch metadata and telemetry link
- POST /routes/{route}/module-config — attach modules and route-level budget/policy
- runtime hook: include module_decisions array in request trace (which module ids used, variant chosen, token delta)

UX/Dev exp notes:
- Provide a small UI in Console: module registry table (owner, triggers, average added tokens, last 7d cost). Quick toggle to enable/disable per-customer.
- Inline playground: run a sample chat and toggle modules to see delta in response. Capture golden prompt snippets for regression evals.
- Templates gallery: shipping a few curated modules (summary-short, concise-qa, source-locator, polite-clarifier).

Runtime implications (high level):
- Planner: must be extremely cheap — a few rules + heuristics, not a full model. Prefer compile-time heuristics for common triggers.
- Execution: prefer to execute modules in parallel where independent; support shallow composition (module outputs passed as context to next module).
- Caching: cache module outputs keyed by stable request fingerprint + module id + model variant to allow reuse across similar requests.
- Batching: modules with similar templates across requests should be batchable; explore grouping by variant + sequence length.

Telemetry & safety:
- Expose per-module metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, avg tokens generated, avg token cost, quality regressions (via eval hooks).
- Safety: modules must be reviewable (human-readable prompt + redactable secrets). Default disallow external code execution in MVP.

Success metrics (initial):
- Developer adoption: 10 teams onboarded to try modules in 3 months
- Latency impact: median added latency from modules <= 120ms for simple modules (target)
- Cost: measurable reduction in app-level token spend vs naive approach (benchmark: 15% lower per-composite-feature)
- Reliability: per-module error < 1%

Open questions / risks:
- How to reason about module composition order and emergent behavior? Planner heuristics might be brittle.
- How to prevent quality regressions when switching variants (high->low fidelity)? Need automatic small-eval or canary with holdback.
- Billing model: charge per module token? per module execution? Blend with existing per-token charging. Simpler for MVP: per-token with module tags.
- Access control: modules might leak PII if misconfigured — need strong review workflow and optional sandboxing for private modules.

Next concrete steps (near term):
- Spike 1: implement module metadata store + simple trigger evaluator (2 engineer-weeks).
- Spike 2: runtime execution path prototype for single module composition + caching (2 engineer-weeks).
- Design: console table + playground mockups (1 designer wk).
- Instrumentation: wire trace fields for module_decisions and cost delta (1 eng wk).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Sync with Mika on cost/telemetry schema (mika.sato@redwood) — ask for sample dashboards.
- Draft Linear ticket: MOD-122 (starter).
- Run a quick user interview session with 3 product teams (growth chatbot, docs assistant, enterprise search) to validate triggers and gating.

Rough constraints:
- Module outputs should be small (<= 120 tokens) to keep cache hit rates high.
- Only support string/structured JSON output types initially.
- No third-party module execution in MVP.

Rough sketch of module JSON record (brainstorm):
- id: string
- owner: string
- triggers: list of predicates (simple ops: contains, length_gt, header_eq, flag_set)
- template: string (prompt template or function descriptor)
- output_type: [text, json]
- fidelity: [high, balanced, low]
- fallback: [skip, default_text, call-module:id]
- estimated_tokens: int

Comments: this tries to balance product flexibility with runtime operational simplicity. Keep the planner rule set intentionally small at launch. Longer term explore model-based planners that can reason about composition and cost tradeoffs.

-- Omar
